 Judgment

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 19.08.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 19.08.2022 at about 1.00pm to 1.05pm, when he was riding his New Jupiter Scooter on Sarjapura Main Road infront of Keerthi Kruhna Apartment from Dhodha Kannahalli side towards Kaikondrahalli, a Lorry bearing No.KA51D4707 SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 5602/2022 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, took suddenly right side towards left without showing any signal and dashed against the petitioner's scooter.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to Manipal Hospital wherein he was treated as an inpatient for 12 days, operated and discharged with advice.
At the time of accident he was a hale and healthy, working as a Security Guard and earring a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA51D4707.
The HSR layout Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.51/2022.

Therefore, the 1st respondent being the Insurer and the 2nd respondent being the owner of the said SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.
5602/2022 offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels.
But the the Respondent No.1 alone filed written statement.
5. The objection of the respondent No.1.
It has stated that the petition is bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
It is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.

The driver of the Tipper Lorry did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident, but it has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of II respondent in respect of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA51D4707.
Further the offending vehicle did not have permit and FC as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
It has contended that the accident occurred due to self fall from scooter.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 5602/2022 and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 19.08.2022 at about 1.00pm to 1.05pm, due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA51 D4707 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?

7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
Dr. Chidanand K.J.C. got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 to P.16.
Mr.Yadunandana H.L.  MRO at Manipal Hospital got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.17 & 18.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 10. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA51D4707, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.11.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination he has stated that, the road is a Two way with center median.
Except this nothing worthwhile is elicited.

He has also got examined the MRO of Manipal hospital as PW.3 and got SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 5602/2022 marked Exs.P.17 &
18 inpatient records 2 in Nos. and Radiology films and reports 7 in Nos.
During his cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.

The Respondent No.1 insurer has contended that there was no DL to the Lorry Driver and the Lorry did not have FC and Permit and also that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
In order to prove the same, they have not led any evidence.

11. On perusal of the documents, it is clear that the FIR was lodged two days after the accident and all other documents at Exs.P.2, 3 spot mahazar, spot sketch are in accordance with the statement of the petitioner.
The wound certificate at Ex.P.6 shows that the petitioner suffered injuries in a Road Traffic Accident dated 19.08.2022.
The police have recorded the statement of witnesses at Ex.P.9 and filed charge sheet at Ex.P.10.
The IMV report shows that the Lorry did not have any visible damages.

Therefore, on the basis of police records and medical records, it is clear that the accident SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 5602/2022 occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA51D4707.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2: In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6.

As per Ex.P.6, the Petitioner has sustained (i)

sentences.text: 13. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed crush injury to right elbow and forearm and left hand.
He further stated that SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 5602/2022 the petitioner is suffering from permanent disability of upper limb at 43% and to whole body at 14.33%.
14. PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that, he has not treated the petitioner.
There is avulsion fracture along with crush injury which was suffered by the petitioner.
The fracture is in the elbow not in the wrist.

Disability:
15. On perusal of the evidence of PW.2 and the fractures suffered by the petitioner, since he was doing Security Guard work which is a manual labor, he requires both his legs and both his hands.
But, since as per the evidence of Doctor, he has suffered crush injury of the upper limb i.e the right elbow and forearm, it will have some affect on his work.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Security Guard at CMG company and also doing part time Zomoto Swiggy job and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
In the cross examination he has admitted that he has quit the job.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/ per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 22 years as could be made out from Ex.P.12/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Manipal Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 19.08.2022 to 01.09.2022 and was SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 5602/2022 diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.7.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous and simple, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.

ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has not produced any medical bills to prove the medical expenses towards his treatment.
During his cross examination he has stated that out of Rs.10,00,000/, Rs.7,00,000/ was paid by the company.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Manipal Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.

Therefore, considering the SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 5602/2022 nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME: On perusal of Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 09.06.2000 and the date of accident is 19.08.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 22 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,02,200/
(Rs.15,500/ x 12 x 18 x 15%= Rs.5,02,200/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:

The Petitioner was aged about 22 years at the time of accident. He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 5602/2022 as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 15% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
 SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 5602/2022 1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/
2.

The Respondents have not proved their defence as discussed above.

Therefore,
the Respondents being the Insurer and the Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,07,700/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Therefore,
the petition needs to SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 5602/2022 be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,07,700/ (Rupees Six Lakhs Seven Thousand and Seven Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
